name: Content Analyzer
description: Structural fact extraction from scraped content. Classifies into categories (fixed taxonomy), assigns tags, extracts key facts (people, licenses, awards, partnerships, offices, contact), and maps source citations. No summaries, opinions, or marketing prose — pure classification and extraction.
usage_notes: MODEL FLOOR — haiku-4-5 is BELOW this module's capability floor. It reads its reference taxonomy doc (master_categories.md) but does NOT comply with it: it fabricates categories instead of assigning from the configured list. Tested 2026-06, reproduced 100% of tries; escalating to sonnet resolves it. MINIMUM MODEL: sonnet. Any template assigning haiku to content-analyzer is misconfigured. (The v1.4.1 vocabulary-fidelity gate loud-fails such entities only when `vocabulary_checks` is configured; the model floor holds regardless of that gate.) max_tokens RECONCILIATION: because the floor is sonnet — a Claude-5 model with adaptive thinking ON by default — the manifest default of 16384 is UNDER-PROVISIONED here. 16384 was sized for haiku (no thinking overhead); sonnet's thinking consumes the budget invisibly, so 16384 can truncate and the skeleton fail-closed guard turns truncation into a run failure. A sonnet template MUST override max_tokens to 32768. The 16384 default (and the 'sized for haiku' wording on the max_tokens/ai_model option descriptions) are legacy haiku-era values, NOT the intended operating point — do not read them as current. Increase max_content_chars for entities with extensive source material (50+ scraped pages). Runs independently of seo-planner. CONTENT GATE (v1.4.3, M2): after the analysis parses, content-analyzer asserts it carries at least one usable extracted value; a valid-but-empty (HOLLOW) analysis fails LOUD with meta.status:'error' (entity turns red) instead of shipping an empty analysis as success — content-writer and seo-planner both serialize the whole analysis_json into their prompt, so a hollow analysis would cascade into a hollow profile. A non-JSON response keeps its existing raw-text path (out of scope). See README.

options.name: ai_model
options.label: AI Model
options.description: Which model to use for content analysis. Haiku is fast and cheap for structured extraction.

options.name: reference_docs
options.label: Reference Documents
options.description: Reference docs for the analysis prompt. Key docs: master_categories.md (fixed taxonomy), master_tags.md (tag list). Upload once, reuse across runs.

options.name: temperature
options.label: Temperature
options.description: LLM temperature for analysis. Lower = more consistent extraction. Default 0.2 for reliable structured output.

options.name: max_tokens
options.label: Max output tokens
options.description: Maximum tokens in the LLM response. Sized for haiku (no thinking overhead); complete analyses on 200+ page inputs run 1.2k-6.6k tokens. If you switch this module to a Claude-5 model (sonnet/opus), adaptive thinking consumes this budget invisibly — raise it or truncation fails the run.

options.name: max_content_chars
options.label: Max content characters
options.description: Truncate assembled source text to this many characters to control token usage.

options.name: vocabulary_checks
options.label: Vocabulary fidelity checks (per-template)
options.description:
Optional, pipeline-agnostic. When set, after analysis the writer validates that every slug assigned at the given analysis_json path exists in the named reference doc (the injected vocabulary). An assigned slug not found in that doc FAILS the entity, and a missing/empty referenced doc fails the run before any LLM call. Leave EMPTY for content types that do not enforce a closed vocabulary — the gate is then inert.

Format: one entry per line, `<analysis_json.path[].slug>=<reference_doc_name>`. The path uses the same `field.subfield[].leaf` walk as content-writer's allowed_slug_paths. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored.

Example for a company-profile pipeline:
    categories.primary[].slug=master_categories.md
    categories.secondary[].slug=master_categories.md
    tags.existing[].slug=master_tags.md

options.name: prompt
options.label: Analysis prompt
options.description: The prompt sent to the AI. Use {entity_content} for scraped content, {doc:master_categories.md} and {doc:master_tags.md} for taxonomy lists, {doc:filename} for other reference docs.
